name: Wisconsin
overview: Wisconsin DNR requires a construction permit before anyone builds, reconstructs, modifies, relocates or replaces an air pollution source. Minor sources are covered by NR 406, PSD by NR 405, and nonattainment NSR by NR 408. Facilities also need an operation permit (NR 407) unless they are exempt. The construction exemptions in NR 406.04 are judged project by project. The operation exemptions in NR 407.03 are judged for the whole facility. Streamlined options include registration operation permits Types A, B, C and G, and general permits for hot mix asphalt plants and rock crushing. Major sources need a Title V (Part 70) permit. Non-Title V operation permits issued after December 2015 generally do not expire. Fees are set in NR 410. Parts of southeastern Wisconsin are ozone nonattainment areas.

permitTypes.name: General exemptions (MTE-based)
permitTypes.description: These exemptions are based on maximum theoretical emissions (MTE) of each pollutant. For construction they are applied to the project; for operation they are applied to the entire facility. Air toxics must also fall below the NR 445 Table A, B or C values, based on stack height. Exempt sources may still need to notify DNR on Form 4530-100.
permitTypes.quote: 9.0 pounds (lb) per hour of sulfur dioxide or carbon monoxide; 5.7 lb/hr of particulate matter (PM), nitrogen oxides (NOx) or volatile organic compounds (VOC); 3.4 lb/hr of PM less than 10 microns in size (PM10); 2.2 lb/hr of PM2.5; 0.13 lb/hr of Lead (Pb)

permitTypes.name: Specific source-category exemptions
permitTypes.description: Covers gaseous-fuel boilers with total heat input under 25 MMBtu/hr; restricted-use reciprocating engines with total electric output under 3,000 kW; painting, coating, graphic arts and refinishing using no more than 1,666 lb of VOC per month before controls; cold cleaning with a total air-to-vapor interface of 1.0 m² or less; dry cleaning up to 75 lb of clothes per hour total capacity; grain storage receiving an average under 5,500 tons per month; grain processing averaging under 4,500 tons per month; and gasoline dispensing. A facility may combine categories for an operation exemption only if NR 407.03(1)(t) lists them.

permitTypes.name: Actual-emissions and natural minor exemptions
permitTypes.description: Three exemptions are available. The controlled actual emissions construction exemption (NR 406.04(1q); fact sheet AM-387) and the actual emissions operation exemption (NR 407.03(1m); fact sheet AM-388) are each explained in a DNR fact sheet. The natural minor operation exemption (NR 407.03(1s)) is not available to a facility whose MTE exceeds Part 70 major source levels. NR 406.04(4) lists exclusions from the definition of modification.

permitTypes.name: Registration Operation Permits (Types A, B, C, G)
permitTypes.description: These are streamlined operation permits for small emitters. Type A (ROP-A) is the simplest option. Type B (ROP-B) has higher eligibility thresholds. Type C (ROP-C) is for printers and allows hazardous air pollutants below 50% of the major source threshold. Type G (ROP-G01/G02) is for Green Tier participants and requires emissions below 80% of major source thresholds. DNR must review each application within 15 days, and the annual fee is $400.
permitTypes.quote: Facilities must have emissions below 25% of the major source threshold for both criteria and hazardous air pollutants.
permitTypes.thresholds: Type A: below 25% of major source thresholds (criteria and HAP). Type B: below 50% (criteria and HAP). Type C: below 25% for criteria pollutants and 50% for HAP. Type G: below 80%, plus Green Tier Tier 2 status (verbatim percentages from DNR's Registration Permit Options page).

permitTypes.name: General Construction and Operation Permits
permitTypes.description: General permits cover hot mix asphalt plants and nonmetallic mineral (rock crushing) plants, and DNR's options page also lists printers. General operation permits do not expire, and DNR must decide within 15 days of submittal. Replacing a primary crusher, or an asphalt plant's drum and burner at the same time, requires a construction permit.

permitTypes.name: Construction Permit (minor source)
permitTypes.description: A construction permit is required before construction, modification, expansion or replacement of a source. DNR's preliminary decision is due within 90 days of a complete application for minor sources, or 120 days for major sources, followed by a 30-day public comment period. Authority to construct lasts 18 months, with one 18-month extension. Fees: a $7,500 application fee is credited against the review bill; minor source review costs $3,000 base plus $800 per emission source when two or more are reviewed, $1,000 for an air quality analysis, and $5,000 for optional expedited review. A construction waiver for undue hardship (NR 406.03(2)) costs $300. Construction permit revisions under NR 406.11(1) use a 21-day notice period.

permitTypes.name: Operation Permit (non-Part 70 minor and synthetic minor)
permitTypes.description: An operation permit covers the entire facility, and it is required unless the facility is exempt. A synthetic minor accepts limits that keep it under major source levels. Limits between 80 and 99 tpy are classed as SM80, and limits below 80 tpy are classed as SM, with lower fees. Non-Title V permits issued after December 2015 generally do not expire.
permitTypes.quote: Anything between 99 tons per year and 80 tons per year is called SM80

permitTypes.name: Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD)
permitTypes.description: This permit covers major sources and major modifications in areas that meet the NAAQS. The DNR pages reviewed do not state numeric PSD thresholds; see ch. NR 405.

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment NSR
permitTypes.description: This permit applies to the 2015 ozone nonattainment areas: all of Milwaukee and Ozaukee counties, parts of Washington, Waukesha and Racine counties, and parts of Sheboygan and Kenosha counties. DNR says it is generally more stringent than PSD. For existing major sources, a project triggers NNSR if its increase exceeds 40 tpy. A Serious reclassification would lower the threshold to 50 tpy, but the Seventh Circuit stayed that reclassification on Sept. 5, 2025, so Moderate requirements currently apply.
permitTypes.quote: the NNSR major source threshold of 100 tons per year

permitTypes.name: Title V (Part 70) Operation Permit
permitTypes.description: Required for major sources. The permit has a five-year term, and renewal applications are due at least 6 months and no more than 18 months before expiration. Annual fees follow the Title V fee schedule.
permitTypes.quote: any single criteria pollutant (PM, SO2, NOX, CO) or volatile organic compounds (VOC) above 100 tons per year ... a single federally regulated hazardous air pollutant above 10 tons per year ... total of all federally regulated hazardous air pollutants above 25 tons per year

oilAndGas.summary: Wisconsin has no oil and gas production air permit program in DNR's air permit pages. Industrial (frac) sand mines and processing plants use the standard construction and operation permits and the nonmetallic mineral general permit.

notes: The exemption thresholds and Title V thresholds are quoted from DNR pages. The PSD numeric thresholds were not shown on the pages reviewed; see NR 405. Registration eligibility is stated only as percentages of major source thresholds. EPA's 'CAA Permitting in Wisconsin' page would not load during review, so the absence of local or tribal permitting authorities is unconfirmed. NR chapter titles are standard titles and should be checked against the Legislature's code site.
